hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to **high-contrast grayscale or monochromatic images** featuring a **dark, central subject** set against a **uniform or textured light gray background**. The activating feature is typically a **vertically oriented structure** or silhouette—such as the elongated body of an insect (spider, centipede, butterfly), a hanging cord, a vertical seam, or an instrument needle—rendered in deep black or charcoal. The neuron is invariant to the semantic category of the object (biological vs. mechanical), texture (smooth, shiny, or grainy), and precise shape, as long as the image remains strictly achromatic and preserves a sharp **dark-on-light luminosity contrast**. The dominant colors are exclusively **black, charcoal, and dark gray** for the subject, set against a background of **light gray, silver, or off-white**. The feature typically occupies **30–70% of the image** and is aligned along the central vertical axis or centered within the frame.

natural.description: A monochromatic, grayscale image captures a waterfowl swimming in calm water, viewed in profile and facing toward the right side. The bird features a rounded head and neck rendered in a deep, dense black that appears smooth and velvety, contrasting sharply with its stout, triangular beak which is bright white. The beak is thick at the base, tapers to a point, and shows a faint dark marking near the tip. Situated just behind the base of the beak is a small, light-colored eye that stands out against the dark plumage of the face. The body of the bird, floating low in the water, is covered in feathers of a lighter, mottled dark grey, displaying a soft, textured appearance along the curved back and flank. The water surrounding the bird is depicted in horizontal bands of varying grey tones, with soft, blurred ripples visible in the background that suggest gentle movement. A faint, thin, vertical line, possibly a reed or reflection, is visible in the water on the left side, positioned behind the bird's tail area. The lighting is diffuse, creating soft highlights on the water's surface and the white beak while keeping the head in deep shadow.

A bird of prey is captured in a ventral view, soaring upwards against a uniform, heavily grainy, medium-gray background that fills the negative space. The bird is centered and oriented vertically, with its small, pale gray head pointing towards the top and its body extending downwards along the central axis. The wings are spread wide, spanning the entire width of the view, with the tips of the primary feathers truncated by the limits of the visible area on both the left and right. The plumage is distinctly patterned: the slender body and the forward coverts of the wings are a deep, dark brown, appearing almost black in the backlit conditions. In high contrast, the underside of the primary flight feathers displays large, translucent white patches on both wings, bordered by dark, finger-like feathers. The tail, extending to the bottom of the view, is a rusty reddish-brown and is deeply forked, though the very ends are cut off by the lower boundary. The texture of the image is coarse, with visible monochromatic noise in the gray sky, and the lighting is diffuse, emphasizing the silhouette and the color variation between the dark body, white wing patches, and rufous tail.

A grayscale close-up captures the midsection and limbs of a reptile, likely a gecko, clinging vertically to a textured surface. The creature's body dominates the right-center, its skin exhibiting a granular, stippled texture with small, raised bumps that catch the light. A faint, darker line runs vertically along the spine. To the left of the reptile, a flat, matte gray wall serves as the background, separated from the animal by a sharp, deep black shadow cast by the reptile's body, indicating a strong light source from the right. Extending from the left side of the reptile's torso is a forelimb, angled downwards and outwards; its foot is splayed with distinct, segmented toes ending in widened pads, gripping the wall. On the right side, partially obscured and positioned slightly lower, a hind limb clings to a vertical structural element. This element, appearing to the right of the reptile, features straight vertical lines and a smoother surface than the wall on the left, suggesting a frame or edge. The lighting creates high contrast, with bright highlights on the right side of the reptile's back and the vertical structure, while the left side of the reptile and the cast shadow are deep blacks. The scene is tightly framed, excluding the head and tail, focusing entirely on the texture of the skin, the grip of the limbs, and the interaction of light and shadow on the vertical surface.

Soft, diffuse shadows fall slightly to the right of the cords and metal pieces, suggesting a light source from the upper left.

Centered on a textured, monochromatic off-white surface is a vertical view of a house centipede, occupying roughly forty percent of the width and seventy percent of the height of the visible area. The arthropod's segmented body is elongated and distinct, featuring a dark charcoal-grey stripe running longitudinally down its center, flanked by lighter grey bands and darker edges. The background is a smooth, featureless blur of medium gray, providing a soft, uniform backdrop that emphasizes the sharp focus and intricate textures of the butterfly and its perch.
